To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have prepared and characterized new uranyl phosphonate lamellar compounds and that the electrical behaviour of these compounds has been studied and compared with that of a protonic conductor.

(1) new uranyl phosphonate compounds have been synthesized and the structure and electrical properties have been determined; (2) the electrical conductivity is higher than that found for other inorganic materials, but lower than that of the protonic conductor (Nafion) used as reference; and (3) the electrical conductivity increases with temperature.
we have synthesized and characterized new phosphonates, which have been studied from a thermal, spectroscopical and electrical point of view.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of inorganic materials with good thermal stability for the fabrication of supported membranes.
the development of a new generation of inorganic supported membranes with a high protonic conductivity and a good thermal stability.
the synthesis and characterization of some uranyl organophosphonates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lamellar phosphonate UO2(O 3PC6H 4NH 2) is a promising material as protonic conductor, but it is not as good as HUP.
the transport of electric charge in UO2 phosphonates is mainly governed by the transport of protons and not by the transport of the uranyl ion, as it is the case of the UO2 phosphates.
the transport properties of UO2(O2PC6H4CH2NH2)(H2O) are very similar to those of HUP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uranyl phosphonate materials have a good protonic conductivity, but they have not the same high values as HUP.
the uranyl phosphonate materials are stable and good proton conductors.
these uranyl phosphonate materials are good protonic conductors, but they are not good ionic conductors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UO2(O2CR)2·xH2O compounds are promising materials for the preparation of supported membranes for fuel cell application.
the lamellar phosphonate [UO2(3PC4H8)] (UPP51) can be used to fabricate membranes for fuel cells with good performance.
UO2(O2PC6H5)(UPP51) is an excellent candidate for proton conduction in the solid state.
